question.:question/problem: If the path $C$ is a part of the parabola $y={x}^{2}$ traversed from the point $A(0,0)$ to point $B(2,4),$ then ${\int }_{C}x\,dx+y\,dy=$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that our curve is given by the explicit Cartesian equation $y={x}^{2}.$ As a result, we obtain the following parametrization of the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t)=x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j=t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j,\,t\in [0,2]\end{aligned}
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=i+2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}x\,dx+y\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t+y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}t\cdot 1+{t}^{2}\cdot 2t\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}t+2{t}^{3}\,dt \\  & ={[\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{t}^{4}}{2}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =[\frac{{2}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{2}^{4}}{2}]-[0] \\  & =2+8 \\  & =10\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}r(t)=x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j=t\,i+(t+1)^{2}\,j,\,t\in [0,1]\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=i+2(t+1)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that our curve is given by the explicit Cartesian equation $y=2 \sqrt{x}.$ As a result, we obtain the following parametrization of the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t)=x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j=\left(t^{2}\right)\,i+\left(2 t\right)\,j,\,t\in [1,2]\end{aligned}
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)&=\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=\left(2 t\right)\,i+\left(2\right)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_C\left(2 x - 2 y\right)\,dx+\left(3 x + 3 y\right)\,dy &={\int }_{1}^{2}\left(2 x - 2 y\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t+\left(3 x + 3 y\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  &={\int }_{1}^{2}\left(\left(2 x - 2 y\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(3 x + 3 y\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)\,dt \\  &={\int }_{1}^{2}\left(2 \left(t^{2}\right) - 2 \left(2 t\right)\right)\cdot \left(2 t\right)+\left(3 \left(t^{2}\right) + 3 \left(2 t\right)\right)\cdot \left(2\right)\,dt \\  &={\int }_{1}^{2}4 t^{3} - 8 t^{2}+6 t^{2} + 12 t\,dt \\  &={\int }_{1}^{2}4 t^{3} - 2 t^{2} + 12 t\,dt \\  &=\left[- \frac{2 t^{3}}{3}+t^{4}+6 t^{2}\right]_{1}^{2} \\  &=[- \frac{2 \left(2\right)^{3}}{3}+\left(2\right)^{4}+6 \left(2\right)^{2}]-[- \frac{2 \left(1\right)^{3}}{3}+\left(1\right)^{4}+6 \left(1\right)^{2}] \\  &=[- \frac{16}{3}+16+24]-[- \frac{2}{3}+1+6] \\  &=\frac{85}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_C\left(\frac{2}{y}\right)\,dx+\left(\frac{2}{x^{2}}\right)\,dy &={\int }_{1}^{3}\left(\frac{2}{y}\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t+\left(\frac{2}{x^{2}}\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  &={\int }_{1}^{3}\left(\left(\frac{2}{y}\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(\frac{2}{x^{2}}\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)\,dt \\  &={\int }_{1}^{3}\left(\frac{2}{\left(t^{3}\right)}\right)\cdot \left(1\right)+\left(\frac{2}{\left(t\right)^{2}}\right)\cdot \left(3 t^{2}\right)\,dt \\  &={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{2}{t^{3}}+6\,dt \\  &={\int }_{1}^{3}6 + \frac{2}{t^{3}}\,dt \\  &=\left[6 t- \frac{1}{t^{2}}\right]_{1}^{3} \\  &=[6 \left(3\right)- \frac{1}{\left(3\right)^{2}}]-[6 \left(1\right)- \frac{1}{\left(1\right)^{2}}] \\  &=[18- \frac{1}{9}]-[6-1] \\  &=\frac{116}{9}\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem: If the path $C$ is a part of the graph $y=2 \sqrt{x}$ traversed from the point $A(0,0)$ to point $B(4,4),$ then ${\int }_C\left(x^{2} + 2 y\right)\,dx+\left(x + y\right)\,dy=$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that our curve is given by the explicit Cartesian equation $y=2 \sqrt{x}.$ As a result, we obtain the following parametrization of the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t)=x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j=\left(t^{2}\right)\,i+\left(2 t\right)\,j,\,t\in [0,2]\end{aligned}
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)&=\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=\left(2 t\right)\,i+\left(2\right)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_C\left(x^{2} + 2 y\right)\,dx+\left(x + y\right)\,dy &={\int }_{0}^{2}\left(x^{2} + 2 y\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t+\left(x + y\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  &={\int }_{0}^{2}\left(\left(x^{2} + 2 y\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(x + y\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)\,dt \\  &={\int }_{0}^{2}\left(\left(t^{2}\right)^{2} + 2 \left(2 t\right)\right)\cdot \left(2 t\right)+\left(\left(t^{2}\right) + \left(2 t\right)\right)\cdot \left(2\right)\,dt \\  &={\int }_{0}^{2}2 t^{5} + 8 t^{2}+2 t^{2} + 4 t\,dt \\  &={\int }_{0}^{2}2 t^{5} + 10 t^{2} + 4 t\,dt \\  &=\left[\frac{t^{6}}{3}+2 t^{2}+\frac{10 t^{3}}{3}\right]_{0}^{2} \\  &=[\frac{\left(2\right)^{6}}{3}+2 \left(2\right)^{2}+\frac{10 \left(2\right)^{3}}{3}]-[\frac{\left(0\right)^{6}}{3}+2 \left(0\right)^{2}+\frac{10 \left(0\right)^{3}}{3}] \\  &=[\frac{64}{3}+8+\frac{80}{3}]-[0+0+0] \\  &=56\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)&=\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=\left(1\right)\,i+\left(2 t - 1\right)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Notice that our curve is given by the explicit Cartesian equation $y=3 \pi x^{2}.$ As a result, we obtain the following parametrization of the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t)=x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j=\left(t\right)\,i+\left(3 \pi t^{2}\right)\,j,\,t\in [1,2]\end{aligned}
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)&=\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=\left(1\right)\,i+\left(6 \pi t\right)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_C\left(\sin{\left(\frac{y}{2 x^{2}} \right)}\right)\,dx+\left(5 x\right)\,dy &={\int }_{1}^{2}\left(\sin{\left(\frac{y}{2 x^{2}} \right)}\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t+\left(5 x\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  &={\int }_{1}^{2}\left(\left(\sin{\left(\frac{y}{2 x^{2}} \right)}\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(5 x\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)\,dt \\  &={\int }_{1}^{2}\left(\sin{\left(\frac{\left(3 \pi t^{2}\right)}{2 \left(t\right)^{2}} \right)}\right)\cdot \left(1\right)+\left(5 \left(t\right)\right)\cdot \left(6 \pi t\right)\,dt \\  &={\int }_{1}^{2}-1+30 \pi t^{2}\,dt \\  &={\int }_{1}^{2}30 \pi t^{2} - 1\,dt \\  &=\left[- t+10 \pi t^{3}\right]_{1}^{2} \\  &=[- \left(2\right)+10 \pi \left(2\right)^{3}]-[- \left(1\right)+10 \pi \left(1\right)^{3}] \\  &=[-2+80 \pi]-[-1+10 \pi] \\  &=-1 + 70 \pi\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}{\int }_C\left(4 x^{2} y\right)\,dx+\left(2 x^{2} \left(y + 1\right)\right)\,dy &={\int }_{1}^{2}\left(4 x^{2} y\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t+\left(2 x^{2} \left(y + 1\right)\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  &={\int }_{1}^{2}\left(\left(4 x^{2} y\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(2 x^{2} \left(y + 1\right)\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)\,dt \\  &={\int }_{1}^{2}\left(4 \left(t\right)^{2} \left(t^{2} - 1\right)\right)\cdot \left(1\right)+\left(2 \left(t\right)^{2} \left(\left(t^{2} - 1\right) + 1\right)\right)\cdot \left(2 t\right)\,dt \\  &={\int }_{1}^{2}4 t^{4} - 4 t^{2}+4 t^{5}\,dt \\  &={\int }_{1}^{2}4 t^{5} + 4 t^{4} - 4 t^{2}\,dt \\  &=\left[- \frac{4 t^{3}}{3}+\frac{4 t^{5}}{5}+\frac{2 t^{6}}{3}\right]_{1}^{2} \\  &=[- \frac{4 \left(2\right)^{3}}{3}+\frac{4 \left(2\right)^{5}}{5}+\frac{2 \left(2\right)^{6}}{3}]-[- \frac{4 \left(1\right)^{3}}{3}+\frac{4 \left(1\right)^{5}}{5}+\frac{2 \left(1\right)^{6}}{3}] \\  &=[- \frac{32}{3}+\frac{128}{5}+\frac{128}{3}]-[- \frac{4}{3}+\frac{4}{5}+\frac{2}{3}] \\  &=\frac{862}{15}\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}r(t)=x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j=\left(t\right)\,i+\left(2 t^{2}\right)\,j,\,t\in [0,1]\end{aligned}
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)&=\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=\left(1\right)\,i+\left(4 t\right)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_C\left(2 y\right)\,dx+\left(3 x\right)\,dy &={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(2 y\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t+\left(3 x\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  &={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(\left(2 y\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(3 x\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)\,dt \\  &={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(2 \left(2 t^{2}\right)\right)\cdot \left(1\right)+\left(3 \left(t\right)\right)\cdot \left(4 t\right)\,dt \\  &={\int }_{0}^{1}4 t^{2}+12 t^{2}\,dt \\  &={\int }_{0}^{1}16 t^{2}\,dt \\  &=\left[\frac{16 t^{3}}{3}\right]_{0}^{1} \\  &=[\frac{16 \left(1\right)^{3}}{3}]-[\frac{16 \left(0\right)^{3}}{3}] \\  &=[\frac{16}{3}]-[0] \\  &=\frac{16}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
